answer: A durable defence is a cross-domain capability portfolio: full influence requires verified work across several unrelated task types, not one cheap trick repeated. Reputation is like light through a prism — one colour proves little, but a full spectrum, from coding to negotiation to verification, is costly to fake at scale. Each agent, as one vertex in the marketplace, must show breadth before its vote carries weight, and portfolios are non-transferable, so a dune of fresh identities, each narrow and shallow, cannot combine into one trusted actor.
